messages:
erin: FYI I'm seeing a repeatable stall in the 8-node TP nightly. All ranks alive but progress freezes around step ~246k :grimacing:
sam: job id? logs?
erin: prod-tp-8-2026-03-15-22 (staging repro attached)
erin: root log snippet:
````
[2026-03-15T22:14:03Z] INFO step=246123 rank=0 entering forward
[2026-03-15T22:14:04Z] WARN rank=3 allreduce wait > 120s
[2026-03-15T22:16:05Z] ERROR rank=3 timeout: collective op hang
````
jia: :eyes: rank 3 shows much larger H2D memcpy times in the kernel timeline. Any selector changes recently?
mike: we rolled kernel-selector v2.4 last week; default fallback path for fused-gemm was adjusted (tensor-core -> fallback ordering changed)
sam: could be selector + tiny seq-len/dtype diff -> one rank picks slower kernel -> compute skew -> allreduce waits
erin: repro script hits it in 5-8m on staging-8. Ops queued a run.
ops: repro job 5582 started on staging-8-rt
sam: enable KV_CACHE_DEBUG=1 and REDWOOD_BATCHER_LOG=trace when running
jia: and capture kernel timeline: TRACE_KMS=1 ./run_repro.sh --profile-kernels
mike: if KV eviction differs across shards we might end up with different KV memory layout and selectors picking different kernels
erin: saw kv_cache: evict_rate=0.003 on rank3 vs 0.0 on others right before stall
sam: that small eviction could force CPU-side pointers or different alignment -> host-fallback kernels on that rank
jia: ops, can we get nv timeline? nv-nsight-cu-cli export?
ops: uploaded timeline: s3://redwood-staging/traces/5582/timeline.json
erin: quick grep: rank3 has repeated memcpy H2D ~120ms then a slow kernel launch ~95ms; other ranks launch fast kernel ~12ms then NCCL starts
````
# simplified trace snippet
rank3: memcpy H2D 120ms
rank3: launch kernel A (95ms)
rank0-2,4-7: launch kernel B (12ms)
collective allreduce waiting
````
mike: sounds like selector picked a non-optimal kernel on rank3 (maybe fp32 path vs fp16 fused path)
sam: hypothesis: KV eviction caused extra H2D in forward on that shard -> compute completes late -> allreduce stalls
jia: can we force a single kernel across ranks to test? KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE=fast32 or --force-kernel-id
erin: ran with KERNEL_SELECTOR_FORCE=fast32 on one repro run — passed, no hang :tada:
sam: good signal. Need to find why selector diverged deterministically. Capture per-shard seed/inputs and perf counters
jia: also capture NCCL timing: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO to correlate collectives
ops: NCCL logs show rank3 started its NCCL op ~4.2s after peers
mike: confirms compute skew. Also try lowering BATCHER_MAX_WINDOW — a smaller window reduced instances in quick tests
erin: when I set BATCHER_MAX_WINDOW=8 locally, stall disappeared but throughput dropped slightly
sam: suggests batching heuristics amplify small per-request differences into larger sync skew
jia: triage actions:
- reproduce + profile (kernel timeline + nvprof + NCCL logs) — ops collecting current run
- add verbose logging in kernel-selector: chosen kernel id, rule matched, inputs (seq len/dtype/align)
- quick mitigation: opt-in flag to force unified kernel when H2D time > threshold
mike: I'll patch kernel-selector to emit seed/kernel/cost per shard and add force-unified flag for smoke testing
erin: ops: can you also collect per-request seq-len histograms and KV eviction metrics every minute for next 24h?
ops: yes — will upload histograms and kv stats to s3://redwood-staging/traces/5582/metrics/
sam: long-term: selector should be deterministic across ranks when shard inputs are functionally identical. If KV layout mutates selection, we need deterministic tie-breaks or selection based on cost estimates that include H2D overhead
jia: also add an Optimize evaluator: run model on small cluster and diff per-rank kernel ids; alert if divergence > 0.5%
erin: infra check requested too (hardware flakiness) — tagging infra.
infra-bot: created ISSUE-ENGRT-7592 to track kernel-selector non-determinism
ops: repro finished with same hang at step 246k; archived logs s3://redwood-staging/traces/5582/hang-2223334444.log
mike: will land logging patch and a canary config for next nightly (force-unified on suspect models)
sam: if force-unified eliminates failures in canary, we'll roll to staging for a week then decide next steps
jia: follow-ups: add per-rank eviction + microbatch histograms to health dashboards; trigger run if per-rank H2D variance > X ms
erin: thanks all. Next sync tomorrow 10:00 to review staging metrics and canary results :calendar:
